resources.string: Uses the system Accessibility Service to find and tap “Skip / Close ad” on your device.
Automatically tap “Skip / Close” on splash and pop-up ads

When enabled, this service reads the on-screen view hierarchy, looks for buttons such as “Skip”, “Skip ad”, “Close ad” and taps them. All matching happens locally on your device. No network access, no data collection, no uploads.
Enabled in system settings, waiting for the system to connect (switch to another app to trigger it)
Tap the button below, then find “AdSkip” under “Downloaded services / Installed services” and turn it on.
Use the master switch below to pause temporarily; disable it in system accessibility settings to stop it completely.
Could not open accessibility settings automatically. Go to Settings → Accessibility.
Loose mode on: ordinary dialog close buttons may also be tapped
When off, nothing is detected or tapped
Matches “Skip”, “Skip ad”, “Skip 3s”, “跳过”. Lowest risk, recommended.
Matches “Close ad”, “Not interested”, and ids like ad_close / iv_close.
Only taps small, clickable, corner-positioned single crosses — for in-app pop-up ads.
Off by default. Also taps ordinary dialog close buttons, so it may over-click.
One package name per line, commas also work. Nothing is ever tapped inside these apps.
System UI, Settings, permission controller, launchers, keyboards, phone / messaging, and major banking / payment apps are never touched.
No records yet. Enable the service and open an app with a splash ad.

· Never taps words like Cancel / OK / Pay / Buy / Agree / Allow / Download / Delete / Sign out
· 0.7 s cooldown per tap, max 25 taps per minute
· The same target is tapped at most once per 1.5 s
· Built-in list of system and payment apps is left completely alone
